editorial.headline: Marketing Consultancy, Nationally Open but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers marketing strategy and brand-development consulting, open nationally to every business scale but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned business cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, it is classified as blocked by risk class: at the Large scale, every scope is assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk and falls within the Bali moratorium.

The activity is marketing and commercial-management consulting. Its work includes giving opinions, advice and studies on developing and analysing marketing strategies; building and developing brands; providing services that improve sales value; and supporting other management functions in marketing. In practical terms, this is the advisory side of marketing: the strategic work of shaping how a business understands its market, develops its brand and strengthens its commercial function.

Nationally, the activity is open across Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. The record sets the maximum foreign ownership at 100%, under the cited national investment framework. That national openness is clear, but it does not displace the Bali position. Bali’s province-wide, permanent rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA, and the Large-scale risk assessment for this activity brings it within that rule.

For founders, the distinction is not a technical footnote. The national investment position describes the ownership ceiling for the activity; Bali’s moratorium determines whether PMA registration is available on the island. Here, the national ceiling is fully open, while Bali blocks the activity for PMA registration because of its risk classification. Any reading of the code needs to hold both facts together.
